title: I guess it is expected for the price
text:
First off, are we still using it or is it an expensive clothes hanger? Hanger. Half is our fault, as we got this to hopefully cancel our gym membership, and we mainly use an elliptical there. And this cannot even come close to the gym's quality equipment. But we expected that. But this machine is as bare bones as they come.

Resistance band is literally a cloth-like material. You make your initial resistance adjustments just as you would on a similarly fashioned pants belt. It comes loose often, and when this happens, it totally lowers the resistance you have set. The quick style resistance control is a knob that is between your legs, and you can feel the difference at the easiest, and at the hardest, but nothing in between. So basically only two resistance settings unless you want to tackle the hard-yo-adjust belt thing.

Also, stability is an issue. If you have a hardwood or concrete floor, sure this won't wobble. But we have the short-cut type of carpet, you know, not the kind long enough to even pinch a fingertip full. It should be more than sturdy to support this machine. And it does, to a point. If you are taking a casual stroll on the thing, it is fine. But if you try upping the RPMs since you cannot get a good resistance, then it wobbles. It hasn't fallen over, thank god, but sometimes it sure does feel like it's going to.

And finally it advertises that it also functions as a bike....and good luck with that. You cannot even get the bike started unless you stand up and use it as an elliptical first. And then after that, it just feels off continuing as a bike. I've been on several different style exercise bikes, and they all feel like you are doing something correct (hard to describe this feeling, and this was the best I could think of to put it into words). This does not. If you are going to get this, just go in thinking you are only getting an elliptical.

Would I buy this again? Absolutely not. Can I recommend this to anyone? It depends. If you know that the only way you are going to exercise at home, and you don't have a lot of money to buy something better, then it could work. But if you have ANY experience exercising on quality equipment, this will not do at all.

title: Re-engineering this product made it a winner!
text:
After reading several negative reviews of these helm chairs breaking, I bought the one used one on Amazon at about one-fourth the full price. I thought there must me some easily correctable flaw. The chair that arrived looked very new with only one minor fabric scuff.

I quickly found the structural flaws and, with about $12 of stainless hardware, corrected the flaws. I replaced the funky ferrous pressed-in prong surface nuts in the white foot base with stainless flat washers and nylon lock nuts. The bolts that mounted the aluminum pedestal to the white plastic base were the wrong chamfer at the bolt head, resulting minimum metal-to-metal contact. I replaced these with the correct bolts. Finally, the mounting of the chair itself to the black plastic rectangle above the pedestal was a mess. Four stainless screws into the plastic chair bottom were the only thing holding the chair in place. No wonder other buyers reported them breaking. By oversize drilling the holes in the black rectangle, new stainless bolts now screw directly into pressed fasteners in the seat bottom. The final result was a good-looking, tough, and mechanically sound helm fishing chair. I anticipate no problems in the future, even with the biggest fishers. So, I now have about $122 into the chair and I'm very happy, though a buyer shouldn't have to re-engeneer a product.

title: Not worth the money
text:
I don't normally write bad reviews. I buy a lot of tech gear and sometimes it's great, but often times I'm underwhelmed, but I usually keep my opinions to myself. In this case, I feel compelled to write a negative review because I tried to get the company to address the issues, but they hid behind their limited warranty period. They replaced the product under warranty originally, but the replacement still had the same problem of audio cutting out sometimes when I turned my head/helmet one way or the other. It seems like either an interference issue or perhaps there are wires inside that maybe didn't get soldered very well? It's hard to tell, because it's a wireless product. They refused to warranty the replacements because by the time they were available again to send to me the original warranty period had expired! They offered a 30% discount off another product, but I wasn't about to waste more money with them if they wouldn't stand behind their overpriced product.

I loved the concept of these Chips because they are about as close to Apple Airpods Pro as you can get in a ski helmet, from a tactical perspective with the charging case. The sound quality is good when they're not cutting out. The phone audio only works in the RIGHT ear and I think my hearing is better in my left ear so that is a real issue for me. I've tried switching them to the other side, but then I keep mixing up the controls. Others have reviewed these and I'm acknowledging the same issue with summoning Siri: It requires a "long press" but if you press too long then you have just shut off the headphones and game over when you were trying to SAVE time by using Siri. A double press of one side would be the best way to summon Siri or they should work with the "Hey Siri" functionality like other Apple headphones, but maybe Apple only allows that for their own products, which would be a shame.

I only ski with music once in a while because I am a volunteer ski patroller and I need to be able to hear my patrol radio. I primarily use these for phone calls, but because the audio only works in one ear and my hearing doesn't seem as good on my right side, these are pretty poor. Also, the auto-off functionality means that they turn off automatically after just a few minutes if I'm not listening to music. That's just dumb, it should be configurable to extend the time out from five minutes to one hour or more or be able to disable the auto-off function completely. I get that this is intended to save battery life, but it makes them pretty useless to me, especially at this price point.

I posted a similar review on OT's website, but they clearly suppressed it as it's not showing there. I hope this review helps others from wasting their money. I'm still searching for a better product (fully wireless helmet audio) with the charging case. I wish Apple would make something like this that could be dropped into a ski helmet or have the headphone. An induction charging case would be great too (a la Airpods).

I was given 3 options.
1. Call Norditrack
2. Have a local repair person fix it, and they would refund me $120.00
3. Complete refund on both the unit and shipping (I would assume the 3 year maintenance plan).

I am giving this 1 star because despite some of the good and bad stories, there should be no reason why this thing should have died.

I am hoping I get a quick response tomorrow and we can work from there.

I will update as we go along.

***************UPDATE

So it was initially decided that the motor was broken on the machine by the technician who was dispatched about a week later. It took about 2 weeks to receive another motor. Add a few days to dispatch another tech at this point we are talking almost a month since the machine has arrived. (I was actually contemplating of just doing a return because it was nearing the time to pay the charge on my credit card.) Back to the story, so the tech shows up, we have the new motor, and an excited mom, I then find out that its not the motor, but the control panel. Again back to square one, another 2 weeks for delivery. Again a couple days to dispatch a technician once the part arrived. Tech arrived installed the new control panel and the machine runs, and hasn't had a problem since. Its been working with no issues for about 2 months now. Mom is happy, but I'm not really sure it was worth it. At this point I can't recommend purchasing this unit through this sales channel. Amazon was perfect but I don't know if it is Norditrack, the warehouse who holds this equipment, XPO who ships this equipment, the tech who installed this equipment... bottom line... a product was purchased for over $700 and it didn't work for almost two months from the day the transaction was completed. We weren't given anything for our troubles. Yes we weren't told "oh well sorry no refunds, all sales are final", we were offered a refund of $120 if we decided to let Norditrack off the hook and go with a local repair person, but there was nothing saying "we are sorry for what happened, the month and a half that was lost will be on us" (the company that failed to delight you as a customer). The only power as a customer is a review, to forewarn others of such an awful experience.

I work in the customer service industry, so I know how hard it can be to please customers. In this case, the product offer and the services to support it were abysmal.

Sincerely,

title: This paddle board has made my summer!
text:
I was river swimming and ended up injuring my foot and the urgent care nurse was telling me about how her inflatable SUP has completely changed her life and she's out on it every weekend. I'm really outdoorsy but hadn't paddle boarded much but took a risk on this board and had it shipped to our beach house for vacation on the ocean the next weekend.

I've had the board almost two months now and take it out several times a week. I actually did have a tiny leak on the side but contacted ROC and they provided the best customer service I've ever had. They immediately responded to my call and email, were really professional and friendly and ended up sending me a new Board. This board comes with a one-year warranty which is awesome.

I like:
-the colors
-it's super lightweight and I don't have much of a problem carrying it from the car to a launch site along with my dog, the paddle, water bottle, etc.
-everyone that's been on it has said that they are impressed with how solid it feels and the stability
-my dog loves it and I'm not worried about any puncture issues and can tie her up to the loop on the back; she's constantly jumping off of it and I can still maintain my balance
-the foot leash is great for the ocean or for connecting tubes
-I've fit another women and 10 year old on the board without a problem and that was a little over 300 pounds
-I can pump it up in 6 minutes (I've timed myself) and it's giving me great muscles
-it works well in the ocean, on lakes and in rivers. I think it works best in rivers though.
-the package - getting the dry bag, paddle, backpack, pump, that you can strap down your stuff in the front
-the paddle is adjustable so I can easily use it standing or make it smaller if I want to paddle seated or on my knees. My kids (ages 8 and 10) can also paddle.
-I've used the SUP with 6 friends who wanted to tube down a river and I'm able to pull them all on the SUP

What I don't like as much:
-I was surprised it had a leak but I think it was a glue issue and the company resolved it right away for me
-while it worked well just paddling in the ocean further out (and was an amazing workout), it did not perform well as a surf board. It nose dived every time you caught a wave and it can whip around really fast with the wind and waves since it's so lightweight

I would definitely invest in this board. Everyone I've gone out with has raved about it. It's the perfect COVID summer activity - outside, socially distanced and you can include friends, family and pets! I've honestly gotten a little obsessed and try to go out several times a week because it's so easy. I have a Prius and it easily fits in the back of the car and I can be paddling in no time. Take down is even easier than set up.

text:
I bought 2 bikes. The first one I got was broken. The cord running from the battery to the motor was completely severed out of the box. The 3rd party seller made me repackage the bike and drop it off at fedex before they would send me a new one. Luckily I ordered 2 days apart because after I assembled the first, I cut up and threw the box away. I had to use the box from the 2nd bike (seller wouldn't provide another). So I repackaged (they asked me to repackage how it showed up which was a ton of zip ties holding it together and foam around parts of the bike) and I drove it to FedEx 20 minutes away.

Once they finally sent me the replacement, it showed up broken too! Unfortunately for me, I thought surely this one wouldn't be broken and cut up and threw away the box again. Idiot! The chain was not on the bike, the handle bar grips were shredded, and the rear tire was not secured properly. After I fixed this, I fired it it up so see an error on the display. After googling and troubleshooting I figured out it's the sensor in the pedals.

I message the seller asking for parts since i knew the headache awaiting trying to return this bike, especially since I didn't have a box. They don't have replacement parts apparently. They said I could take it to a bike shop and they would reimburse me. I called all the bike shops in town and none will touch the electronics.

So the seller wants me to return the bike. The gave me a shipping label. I told them I don't have the box and they should send me another. They don't have spare boxes. They told me to buy one from fedex, and they haven't offered to repay me for the cost of the box. They even had the audacity to tell me to buy a sturdier box than the one it came in! Maybe they should take their own advice since I've read quite a few reviews with bikes being damaged upon delivery. I don't think I'm being unreasonable in asking them to send me a box.

Now my wife's bike arrived and it works, luckily. I will say that all 3 bikes I've dealt with aren't exactly ready out of the box after assembly. You will need to readjust the brakes and brake levers. The one thing I also don't understand is the battery meter fluctuates constantly going up and down. I also got the meter to 0% and it still worked for a while so it's completely unreliable and you don't truly know how much battery you have. I will say the bike is fairly smooth and the motor does work well. I live in a very hilly area and it powers up the steep hills no problem.

To sum it up, it works well if you don't get one that's damaged upon arrival. It seems like a coin flip. Buyer beware.

I purchased this racket to replace my Dunlop MaxTack Pro Spin which sadly bit the dust. I purchased this racket based of the reviews found here and other sites. I am a longtime player that relies on spin and control to set up smashes or otherwise create unplayable returns. My game style is to serve the ball so that if returned it will very likely be in a certain quadrant so I can crush the return. For volleys I tend to gain control of the spin by either adding to or reversing it until my opponent cannot return the ball.

I've played 5 matches with it and am very unsatisfied.

Pros: Defending smashes is easier as the racket absorbs a lot of the impact. It also comes with a case, albeit cheaply made.

Cons:
When attacking the ball it provides very little additional spin. I play so that most returns come to my backhand with increasing amounts of top or bottom spin to cause the ball to be returned to me high enough to make my opponent eat it. Intentionally hitting the ball into the net on a serve results in less spin than I can create with the paddles that came with the table.

The racket itself is made of plywood and is poorly finished. Yes, it is a $50 racket, but the bottom of the blade near the grip should not be sharp enough to cut your hand! It is quite loud when striking the ball, doesn't affect play but is annoying. The edging tape was already peeling off when I pulled it out of the case for the first time so QA is a real problem.

Don't waste your money on this one folks. I've played with fiberglass, sand paper, pips in/out, rubber so tacky you can pick a ball off the table with it and I would rate this between sandpaper and pips out.

text:
This bike rack started out fairly strong -- good price and did the job. We ran into some kinks getting the anti-wobble bolt set up, but got them worked out. Worked well for the first couple of outtings. On about the 4th trip, we ran into workmanship issues. Very shortly after that, one of the plastic clips that you secure the main bike-frame straps to broke when we were tightening the bikes down.

As of now, we have a pretty significantly rocking rack that we need to incorporate external straps on and likely will need to purchase a separate anti-wobble bolt to get this back to operational. I wouldn't be comfortable with either our hybrids or road bikes on this rack in current state, and so I'm on here shopping for a new rack that will last more than one short season.

I've contacted Allen who state they have a lifetime warranty on these, so I'll update once I hear back on whether they can take care of the issues.

[Edit] Allen promptly sent out a replacement anti-wobble bolt and tie-down harness (not yet received) free of charge. Still bummed out about the issues, but pleasantly surprised at the ease of getting this taken care of. Now I need to decide if I'm going to take my chances with this or just upgrade to something a little beefier (and significantly pricier). For the price, I think this is a pretty good unit and good service from Allen, but you get what you pay for and I'll likely end up buying a nicer unit to ensure our bikes are 'in good hands'.
